questions.q: Which Power BI component do you use to build and design reports?
questions.explain: Power BI Desktop is the free Windows application where data modeling and report design happen. The service is for publishing and sharing what Desktop builds.

questions.q: How much does Power BI Desktop cost?
options: Nothing — it is a free, fully featured download
It is free for 60 days, then requires a Pro license
questions.explain: Desktop is free with no feature-limited tiers. Licensing costs apply to sharing through the Power BI service, not to building in Desktop.

options: A single screen of pinned visuals
Published, prepared data that reports are built on
The formula language used for calculations
questions.explain: The semantic model (formerly 'dataset') is the reusable prepared data. Reports are built on models; dashboards pin visuals from reports.

questions.q: What is the difference between a report and a dashboard?
options: They are two names for the same thing
A report is interactive pages on one model; a dashboard is one screen of tiles pinned from one or more reports
A report can only show one visual at a time
A dashboard is built in Desktop; a report is built in the service
questions.explain: Reports (built in Desktop, on one semantic model) are for exploring. Dashboards (assembled in the service, from any number of reports) are for monitoring.

questions.q: Which of these is the correct order of the Power BI workflow?
questions.explain: You get the data, clean it with Power Query, model relationships and calculations, build visuals, and publish to the service — the order this course follows.
